title: Two camps on a ring of six?
hook: Two enemy links on a ring of six, plus one cross link. Can two camps form?

knows: two camps = friends inside, enemies across
doesNotKnow: that a network with missing links can be split into two camps exactly when every loop has an even number of enemy links

misconception: If the big loop around everyone looks fine, the network can be split into two camps.
objective: The learner can explain that each enemy link on a loop switches camp, so a loop with an odd number of enemy links returns you to the start in the wrong camp, and that every loop, not only the biggest, must be even for a two-camp split.

claims.text: On the stage (ring A-F plus cross link A-D, enemies A-B and D-E) the big ring has 2 enemy links and each of the two smaller loops made by the cross link has 1.
claims.source: enemyCount() in Demo.tsx; builder re-run in node 2026-10-14 (brief 8 graph: ring 0-5, chord 0-3, enemies 0-1 and 3-4): ring 2, loops 0-1-2-3 and 0-3-4-5 one each. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own count (scratchpad fc22/sg.mjs): ring has enemies A-B, D-E = 2; loop A-B-C-D has A-B = 1; loop A-D-E-F has D-E = 1.

claims.text: None of the 64 ways to put the six people into two camps keeps every friend pair together and every enemy pair apart; the best breaks 1 link (drawn thick, with the two camps as filled and dotted circles).
claims.source: tryAll(ENEMIES_AS_GIVEN) in Demo.tsx, brute force over 2^6 = 64 labellings; builder re-run in node 2026-10-14: 0 valid, minimum 1 broken link. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own brute force over 64 labellings, 7 links: 0 valid, minimum 1 broken. | v2: caption now names the camps and the thick broken link. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Own brute force over 64 labellings, 7 links: 0 valid, minimum 1 broken (best camp 0,1,1,1,0,0 breaks A-D); moved enemy: 2 valid. Caption names filled vs dotted camps and the thick link.

claims.text: With the enemy link moved from D-E to C-D every loop is even (2, 2 and 0), and 2 of the 64 labellings work: one split, with the camp names swapped.
claims.source: tryAll(ENEMIES_MOVED) in Demo.tsx; builder re-run in node 2026-10-14: 2 labellings ({A,D,E,F} vs {B,C} and its swap). Brief 8 edit: 2 labellings, one split. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own brute force with enemies A-B, C-D: loops 2, 2, 0; 2 valid labellings, both the split {A,D,E,F} vs {B,C}.

claims.text: Walking round a loop, every enemy link switches camp and every friendly link keeps it, so a loop with an odd number of enemy links brings you back to the start in the other camp. On stage: walking the right loop or the left loop from A comes back to A in the other camp (clash); walking the big ring comes back in the same camp.
claims.source: Parity argument: the camp after k switches is the start camp iff k is even. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Parity argument re-derived: k switches return to the start camp iff k is even. | v2: Demo.tsx walk(): right loop A B C D with enemy A-B returns camp 1; left loop A D E F with enemy D-E returns 1; ring returns 0. With the enemy on C-D the right loop returns 0. Builder's trace by hand 2026-10-14. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 24): VERIFIED. Parity re-derived; own node walk(): given layout ring 2 enemies back 0, right loop 1 back 1, left loop 1 back 1; moved: right 2 back 0, left 0 back 0. Non-blocking note: after 'Try all 64 splits' the stage shows the best split, not the walk, so a learner who tries all first and then picks loops never sees a walk drawn, though the reveal says 'On those walks'. Demo-standard question for the builder, not a fact error.

claims.text: A network splits into two camps (friends inside, enemies across) exactly when every loop has an even number of enemy links.
claims.source: Easley and Kleinberg (2010) ch. 5 (balance in general networks); F. Harary, 'On the notion of balance of a signed graph', Michigan Math. J. 2 (1953). Attribution: fact-checker confirms (flag carried from the brief). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own check on 3,000 random signed graphs (3-6 nodes): two-camp split exists iff every simple cycle has an even number of negative edges, 0 mismatches. Harary, Michigan Math. J. 2(2):143-146 (1953) confirmed as bibliographic data via search snippets; paper NOT opened. E&K ch. 5 (Positive and Negative Relationships; general-network balance in its advanced section) agrees with my knowledge of the book.

recall.question: A friendship network has several overlapping loops. The biggest loop has 4 enemy links; one small loop inside it has 3. Can the people split into two camps, friends inside and enemies across?
options: Yes, the biggest loop is even
No, the small loop is odd
Only if the network has no small loops at all
recall.why: Each enemy link switches camp. Going round the small loop switches 3 times and lands you in the other camp from where you started, so no split works. Every loop must be even.
